verdict: Caution: lend selectively in Mandideep engineering only to order-backed, export-linked component makers with tight monthly cash monitoring; avoid pure local-demand EPC and small fabricators until MP GST turns positive.
title: Mandideep Engineering & Capital Goods: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Mandideep engineering runs on converting steel, castings and bought-out components into machinery, structures and job-work for OEMs and projects, and cash comes back only after dispatch, inspection and retention release.** The value sits in the order book and the customer relationship, not the shed; pricing power is thin on job-work and stronger only where the unit is a sole-source vendor. Capex is lumpy (casting, machining, fabrication lines) and is usually committed before orders convert, so **when a proposal lands, check whether capex is backed by a signed order or only by intent; if only intent, ask for the customer LOI and the phase-wise commissioning plan.** [4][11]

## Where cash sits and what has changed
**Working capital is the whole game: receivables plus inventory minus payables, and EPC-type work carries a longer cash conversion cycle than OEM supply.** [9][11] Peer results show demand is real but margins are not keeping pace — Pitti is expanding through FY 2030 on data-centre, mining and railway order visibility while flagging margin strain [4], and Suzlon grew revenue 26% to Rs 4,869 crore in Q2 FY27 with EBITDA almost flat at Rs 720 crore and margin down to 14.8% from 18.6% [7]. **So when a proposal lands, check whether volume growth is being bought with price; if EBITDA margin is falling while sales rise, ask for the customer-wise price list and any fixed-price contracts.** [7]

## The local signal versus the national one
**The national picture is strong — IIP NIC 28 output +10.3% YoY and +10.4% Apr-to-date, exports +19.8% Apr-to-date in USD [D] — but Madhya Pradesh GST collections are -0.1% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, a 6.2 pp gap [D].** That gap is the reason this is a Caution call and not a green one. **So treat the corridor as upside, not as a repayment source; if a borrower cites it, ask for the land or allotment document.** [1]

## Who to pursue now, and how to grow safely
**Pursue tier-2 component and structure makers with export or PSU-order linkage, and job-workers supplying named OEMs with a record of on-time dispatch.** Skipper's highest-ever Q2 revenue with PAT up 56% and export growth [6], and DEE's order book above Rs 1,300 crore with Q3 revenue up 77% to Rs 286.7 crore [5], show where order visibility exists. **Avoid pure local-demand fabricators, single-customer units and anyone bidding EPC on bank guarantees alone.** [9] Structure every limit with a cash-flow sweep and a receivables-backed drawing power; take stock and book-debt statements monthly, GST returns monthly, and a quarterly order-book certificate. **If a unit's order book is rising but monthly GST outflow is flat or falling, ask for the dispatch register and the customer confirmation.** [D]
watch: GST outflow flat or falling while sales rise -> ask for dispatch register and customer confirmation
Order book falls or single customer exceeds half -> reduce limit at renewal
Margin down with flat volumes -> reprice or exit at next review
MP GST stays negative while India grows -> hold new-to-bank local-demand EPC

news_why: MP GST -0.1% vs India +6.1% signals local demand stress despite strong national IIP.
